speaker: Steve Holmes
sentence: Wilco set me on a path to rediscover the guitar, standard tuning, and just great songwriting.

speaker: Panda Bear (Noah Lennox)
sentence: That and Aphex Twin really changed the course of my musical life.

speaker: at-the-drive-in
sentence: This is the band that taught me about world influence; it is not just the music but the intent.
citation: Jim Ward of At the Drive-In and Sparta, choosing The Clash's Combat Rock for Spin's "5 Albums I Can't Live Without" (2026): "This is the band that taught me about world influence; it is not just the music but the intent... As I learned more about the Clash and the reach they had, it changed my direction."

speaker: at-the-drive-in
sentence: I learned to play bass by playing along with the Pixies and Dead Kennedys.
citation: Jim Ward of At the Drive-In and Sparta, in Spin's "5 Albums I Can't Live Without" (2026): "I learned to play bass by playing along with the Pixies and Dead Kennedys."
note: Said in the intro answers, not under a pick.

speaker: belle-and-sebastian
sentence: They were a real guide and made me think, "We need to get back to playing simple music again."
citation: Stuart Murdoch, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2015): "They were a real guide and made me think, 'We need to get back to playing simple music again.'"

speaker: Steve Albini
sentence: My favorite bands during that era include those mentioned above, and local/regional bands that inspired me like Naked Raygun, the Effigies, the Appliances, Killdozer, Die Kreuzen, Bad Brains, the Minutemen, Scrawl, Man-Sized Action, the Blackouts, MX-80, Chrome and a bunch of overseas bands like the Birthday Party, Killing Joke, the Bishops, Dr. Feelgood, the Raincoats, Kleenex, Delta Five, Ut, Contortions, Sonic Youth, Swans, Public Image Ltd, This Heat.

speaker: Steve Albini
sentence: My favorite bands during that era include those mentioned above, and local/regional bands that inspired me like Naked Raygun, the Effigies, the Appliances, Killdozer, Die Kreuzen, Bad Brains, the Minutemen, Scrawl, Man-Sized Action, the Blackouts, MX-80, Chrome and a bunch of overseas bands like the Birthday Party, Killing Joke, the Bishops, Dr. Feelgood, the Raincoats, Kleenex, Delta Five, Ut, Contortions, Sonic Youth, Swans, Public Image Ltd, This Heat.

speaker: Cameron Picton of black midi
sentence: When I was younger, I had a neighbor who taught me guitar. He showed me all this Bert Jansch stuff, like "Black Waterside" and all that. I got really into it.
citation: Cameron Picton of black midi, to Stereogum (2021), on what went into Cavalcade: "He showed me all this Bert Jansch stuff, like 'Black Waterside' and all that. I got really into it." He says he went back to Jansch and John Renbourn while arranging in lockdown.

speaker: Graham Coxon
sentence: Things like Robert Wyatt, Van der Graaf Generator and The Velvet Underground really excited me.

speaker: bon-iver
sentence: Radiohead is one of my favorite bands ever. I am truly inspired by their endless innovation.
citation: S. Carey of Bon Iver, choosing Radiohead's Kid A and Amnesiac for Spin's "5 Albums I Can't Live Without" (2022): "Radiohead is one of my favorite bands ever. I am truly inspired by their endless innovation."
note: Present-tense admiration ("inspired by"), not tied to a period of his own making; borderline.

speaker: Brian Eno
sentence: When I heard this record I really thought that I’ve got to change what I’m doing. But the change was actually to do with recording practices as much as anything else.
citation: Brian Eno, choosing Court And Spark by Joni Mitchell for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "When I heard this record I really thought that I've got to change what I'm doing," the change being in recording practice, while making Another Green World.

speaker: Richard H. Kirk of Cabaret Voltaire
sentence: I was a Bowie fan from about 15. I went to see the Ziggy Stardust tour in Sheffield and was kind of blown away as much by the way he looked.
citation: Richard H. Kirk of Cabaret Voltaire, choosing David Bowie's Low for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I was a Bowie fan from about 15."
note: marginal: fan in formative years; Low itself is described as a turning point for electronic music

speaker: Chan Marshall (Cat Power)
sentence: I loved that fucking record, that tape, so much. It was my 12th birthday, and everything was great, it was madness. All these impossible sounds were making sense
citation: Chan Marshall (Cat Power), choosing Hüsker Dü's Metal Circus, given to her at 12 for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I loved that fucking record, that tape, so much. It was my 12th birthday, and everything was great... All these impossible sounds were making sense"
note: marginal: fan in formative years, nothing explicit about her own music

speaker: Robin Guthrie
sentence: I liked all the early punk—Buzzcocks, the Pistols and The Clash, before it all went commercial, when Sham 69 counted as punk.

speaker: descendents
sentence: I started out with X, and then I graduated to the Germs, and then Black Flag.
citation: Milo Aukerman, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2016): "I started out with X, and then I graduated to the Germs, and then Black Flag."
note: "So I went from being obsessed with L.A. punk rock to being a part of it." Strict reading: scene-level obsession just before joining the Descendents.

speaker: destroyer
sentence: At 15, I was deep in the clutches of the Jesus and Mary Chain.
citation: Dan Bejar, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2012): "At 15, I was deep in the clutches of the Jesus and Mary Chain."
note: "That was the first noisy thing I liked"; formative taste, not tied explicitly to his own music.

speaker: Ian McCulloch of Echo & the Bunnymen
sentence: It was Bowie was who got me interested in music, then I got into the Velvets and Iggy.
citation: Ian McCulloch of Echo & the Bunnymen, choosing Hunky Dory by David Bowie for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "It was Bowie was who got me interested in music, then I got into the Velvets and Iggy."

speaker: Will Sergeant of Echo & the Bunnymen
sentence: I learnt all the wobbly guitar sounds you hear on the Bunnymen records from this. I’ve been living off that ever since, really.
citation: Will Sergeant of Echo & the Bunnymen, choosing Television's Marquee Moon for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I learnt all the wobbly guitar sounds you hear on the Bunnymen records from this. I've been living off that ever since, really."

speaker: Ethel Cain
sentence: I was no longer listening to crazy heavy synth electronic music; I was listening to Nicole Dollanganger and Grouper and Slowdive and Def Leppard…

speaker: Robin Pecknold (reported by Missoula Independent)
sentence: Pecknold said that he grew up listening to the music of his parents, who repeatedly played just about every lasting ‘60s band you would expect to find in the record anthologies of baby boomers: The Beach Boys, The Beatles, Simon and Garfunkel, The Band, The Zombies, Joni Mitchell, Bob Dylan, Crosby, Stills and Nash.

speaker: Cameron Winter
sentence: I’ve always liked bands like Television that shout out locations in New York.

speaker: Dazed (reporting Grimes)
sentence: On a more positive note, Grimes gets to express her love for Burial , one of her “all-time favourite artists”, and cites the elusive London producer among artists she considers herself a descendent of ( Aphex Twin and Animal Collective included).

speaker: Alexis Taylor of Hot Chip
sentence: Neil Young was the first songwriter whose songs I learned to play on the guitar.
citation: Alexis Taylor of Hot Chip, choosing Neil Young's On The Beach for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "Neil Young was the first songwriter whose songs I learned to play on the guitar."

speaker: interpol
sentence: Nirvana helped me understand that music was what I wanted to do with my life.
citation: Paul Banks, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2018): "Nirvana helped me understand that music was what I wanted to do with my life."

speaker: Michelle Zauner of Japanese Breakfast
sentence: My other big influence on [For Melancholy Brunettes (& Sad Women)] was Sufjan Stevens’ Carrie & Lowell.
citation: Michelle Zauner of Japanese Breakfast, choosing Sufjan Stevens' Carrie & Lowell for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "My other big influence on [For Melancholy Brunettes (& Sad Women)] was Sufjan Stevens' Carrie & Lowell."

speaker: kurt-vile
sentence: I like a lot of the Guided By Voices.

speaker: James Murphy
sentence: Between the age of 13 and 16 I liked The Clash, Bowie, Echo And The Bunnymen, The Cure, The Smiths, Sisters Of Mercy, Joy Division and New Order.

speaker: liz-phair
sentence: Guyville wouldn’t be Guyville without the Human League.
citation: Liz Phair, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2023): "Guyville wouldn’t be Guyville without the Human League."
note: "It also became really formative for me, because it was the first time I had heard a woman clapping back in a song."

speaker: Alan Sparhawk of Low
sentence: I remember learning the chords to that song on the guitar, and that was the big lightning bolt going on.
citation: Alan Sparhawk of Low, choosing The Clash's Combat Rock for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen, on learning "Should I Stay Or Should I Go?": "I remember learning the chords to that song on the guitar, and that was the big lightning bolt going on."

speaker: mary-timony
sentence: That totally changed my life, and after that, I went to every punk show that was going on and hung out with punk kids.
citation: Mary Timony, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2014): "That totally changed my life, and after that, I went to every punk show that was going on and hung out with punk kids."
note: Her first punk show, Rites of Spring and Beefeater, Jan 1985; "my favorite band from that time was Rites of Spring, and it still is."

speaker: Mike Watt of Minutemen
sentence: When D’s mom makes us into a band and puts me on bass (I bought my first bass for $100), I had to learn bass from Fun House, Creedence and the brothers doing R&B, or like Trevor Bolder [of Bowie’s Spider From Mars and Uriah Heep], because you could really hear the bass on British rock & roll – most US rock & roll buried the bass in the mix.
citation: Mike Watt of Minutemen, choosing The Stooges' Fun House for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen, said that when he was put on bass, "I had to learn bass from Fun House, Creedence and the brothers doing R&B", and that Fun House was "a freak out moment for us" and "the lingua franca" of their scene.

speaker: Stuart Braithwaite of Mogwai
sentence: So Bowie is one of the people who made me consider that I liked music. It was a really important, formative thing.
citation: Stuart Braithwaite of Mogwai, choosing Low by David Bowie for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "Bowie is one of the people who made me consider that I liked music. It was a really important, formative thing."

speaker: my-bloody-valentine
sentence: Basically, we started out as a band that was really into The Birthday Party and Einstürzende Neubauten.

speaker: Kevin Barnes
sentence: Yeah, definitely David Bowie, Prince, Kate Bush, Iggy Pop, Lou Reed, John Lennon, Leonard Cohen, Ray Davies, Skip Spence, Patti Smith, Sly Stone, Fairport Convention, George Clinton, Richard Hell, Wayne County, Screaming Jay Hawkins…

speaker: pavement
sentence: This album was a gateway towards sarcasm and questioning authority and the rightwing and Ronald Reagan – our Margaret Thatcher. I was listening to them in mid-late high school, 1981-82.
citation: Stephen Malkmus, in the Observer's Soundtrack of My Life (2013): on the Dead Kennedys' Fresh Fruit for Rotting Vegetables, from his high-school years: "This album was a gateway towards sarcasm and questioning authority ... I was listening to them in mid-late high school, 1981-82."

speaker: Mike Hadreas
sentence: She was kind of my first true obsession.

speaker: Joey Santiago of Pixies
sentence: That probably seeped in to [his and Black Francis’ playing] on ‘Monkey Gone To Heaven’ through osmosis.
citation: Joey Santiago of Pixies, choosing Television's Marquee Moon for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen, said its trading of rhythm and lead "probably seeped in" to his and Black Francis's playing on "Monkey Gone To Heaven" "through osmosis".
note: Hedged ('probably', 'we didn't mean it'); Marquee Moon was heard after Pixies had started. Owner may prefer favourite.

speaker: Mark Webber of Pulp
sentence: It was records like this that I aspired to make when I was young.
citation: Mark Webber of Pulp, choosing Third/Sister Lovers by Big Star for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "It was records like this that I aspired to make when I was young."

speaker: rem
sentence: There were all these records that came out around then that were so profoundly important.
citation: Michael Stipe, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2021): "There were all these records that came out around then that were so profoundly important."
note: Names Wire's 154 in the same passage ("That was very shocking"); the sentence covers the group of records, not Wire alone.

speaker: sex-pistols
sentence: And I had little time for what was coming out of America; bands like Television never really grabbed me, I just couldn’t connect.
citation: John Lydon, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2016): "And I had little time for what was coming out of America; bands like Television never really grabbed me, I just couldn’t connect."
note: Says they "never really grabbed me"; not a denial of influence in so many words, but he rules them out.

speaker: David Pajo of Slint
sentence: I don’t listen to this record as much as I used to in the early to mid-80s, but it was one of those life-altering LPs in that I was never the same afterwards.
citation: David Pajo of Slint, choosing Out Of Step by Minor Threat for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "it was one of those life-altering LPs in that I was never the same afterwards."

speaker: Neil Halstead of Slowdive
sentence: This was a massive influence on Pygmalion. It’s all about the way they used the space and how it slides into abstraction at points.
citation: Neil Halstead of Slowdive, choosing Spirit of Eden by Talk Talk for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "This was a massive influence on Pygmalion. It's all about the way they used the space and how it slides into abstraction at points."

speaker: Lee Ranaldo of Sonic Youth
sentence: In the late 70s, I was moving to New York and I was inspired by all this stuff coming out of CBGB’s, and Talking Heads was one of the hugest influences at that time.
citation: Lee Ranaldo of Sonic Youth, choosing Talking Heads: 77 by Talking Heads for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "Talking Heads was one of the hugest influences at that time."

speaker: sonic-youth
sentence: For kids of my generation, they (along with Dylan) were the life-changing event.
citation: Lee Ranaldo, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2012): "For kids of my generation, they (along with Dylan) were the life-changing event."
note: Childhood; "To me, Dylan's music is the paramount musical expression of a single individual."

speaker: spiritualized
sentence: I got lucky, because my whole life premise and what I do is kind of built around that record.
citation: Jason Pierce (J Spaceman), in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2012): "I got lucky, because my whole life premise and what I do is kind of built around that record."

speaker: spoon
sentence: When that moment hit me I was just finding out about Eric B. & Rakim, The Beastie Boys were just coming out, I was really into The Cure.
citation: Britt Daniel of Spoon, in NME's Soundtrack Of My Life (2020), on turning 15 in Texas: "I was really into The Cure."
note: Passing mention of fandom at 15; thin, owner may prefer favourite.

speaker: Michael Gira
sentence: I listened to a wide variety of music then ­ The Stooges, Suicide, Throbbing Grist"le, SPK, Cabaret Voltaire, Whitehouse, Brian Eno, Kraftwerk, No New York , Wire, Sex Pistols, Buzzcocks, Black Flag.

speaker: Michael Gira
sentence: I listened to a wide variety of music then ­ The Stooges, Suicide, Throbbing Grist"le, SPK, Cabaret Voltaire, Whitehouse, Brian Eno, Kraftwerk, No New York , Wire, Sex Pistols, Buzzcocks, Black Flag.

speaker: Michael Gira
sentence: I listened to a wide variety of music then ­ The Stooges, Suicide, Throbbing Grist"le, SPK, Cabaret Voltaire, Whitehouse, Brian Eno, Kraftwerk, No New York , Wire, Sex Pistols, Buzzcocks, Black Flag.

speaker: Paul Buchanan
sentence: But there were some great things. The Clash. The Pistols, the Talking Heads, and Television. I suppose we were at the right age as well.

speaker: Brix Smith Start (The Fall)
sentence: I think this is the album that made me want to play bass. It made me sit up and say, ‘I want to be in a band.’
citation: Brix Smith Start (The Fall), choosing Joy Division's Unknown Pleasures for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I think this is the album that made me want to play bass. It made me sit up and say, 'I want to be in a band.'"

speaker: the-national
sentence: Neil Young and Bob Dylan, those kinds of guys.

speaker: Ben Gibbard to The Ringer, 2023
sentence: We were in the right place at the right time to resurrect the craftsmanship of that early ’80s electronic music via Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark, Depeche Mode, or the Human League.

speaker: The Radio Dept. (band site)
sentence: INFLUENCES (the band's own list on its 2007 site)

speaker: Johnny Marr of The Smiths
sentence: As a young guitar player, discovering 154 showed me a world that was an alternative way of looking at the instrument. It has stuck with me all the way through my career.
citation: Johnny Marr of The Smiths, choosing Wire's 154 for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "As a young guitar player, discovering 154 showed me a world that was an alternative way of looking at the instrument. It has stuck with me all the way through my career."

speaker: the-stone-roses
sentence: We couldn't wait for the LP and when it came out it blew us away. I still think it's the best UK album ever made.
citation: Ian Brown, in the Observer's Soundtrack of My Life (2010): on the Sex Pistols at 14: "We couldn't wait for the LP and when it came out it blew us away. I still think it's the best UK album ever made."
note: Formative fandom at about 14, before the band; Brown says the whole run of singles was bought on release day.

speaker: Justin Trosper (Unwound)
sentence: Well I like guitar music alot. Should I list my influences? Greg Ginn(black flag), Sonic Youth, Greg Sage(wipers), Jimi Hendrix, David Lester(mecca normal), Helios Creed(chrome), Tom Verlaine(televison), Toni Iommi(black sabbath) and more.

speaker: Katie Crutchfield
sentence: R.E.M. was a big influence. I saw R.E.M. on their last tour, in an arena.

speaker: WRSU (reported, on Xandy Chelmis)
sentence: Before he fell in love with Jason Molina and Jeff Tweedy, there were Neil Young LPs and Dr. Demento radio sets.

speaker: Graham Lewis of Wire
sentence: He’s in Wire’s minimalism, and you can see his influence go right through – I’m not saying people are trying to emulate him, but you can see it in Earth, in Sunn O))), it’s there.
citation: Graham Lewis of Wire, choosing Neil Young's After The Gold Rush for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "He's in Wire's minimalism, and you can see his influence go right through"

speaker: wire
sentence: At the time being a Nick Drake fan was a very lonely life, but I was always into him.
citation: Colin Newman of Wire, in NME's Soundtrack Of My Life (2015), on buying an Island sampler with Nick Drake on it as his first album: "At the time being a Nick Drake fan was a very lonely life, but I was always into him."
note: Thin: a youthful fan, no link to Wire's own music stated.

speaker: Jamie Stewart of Xiu Xiu
sentence: When I was in 10th grade, I listened to ‘Kiss Me Kiss Me Kiss Me’ every single night before I went to bed for an entire year.
citation: Jamie Stewart of Xiu Xiu, choosing The Cure for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "When I was in 10th grade, I listened to 'Kiss Me Kiss Me Kiss Me' every single night before I went to bed for an entire year."
note: marginal: the 10th-grade line is about Kiss Me Kiss Me Kiss Me, not the picked compilation
